# agents

The coordinator, and a producer and a strictly adversarial reviewer for each of the 9 phases: 19 agents. Generated by `scripts/build-agents.py` from [data/skill-principle-map.json](../data/skill-principle-map.json), [data/taxonomy.json](../data/taxonomy.json), [data/principles.json](../data/principles.json) and the skills; run it after changing any of them.

Each agent's front matter declares `skills` (the skill IDs it loads), `principles` (the principle IDs it can look up) and `loads` (the `SKILL.md` sections it takes from each skill). A phase loads the skills whose `phase` in the skill map is that phase. Producers load each skill's Do and Don't lists together. Reviewers load only the adversarial reviewer checks and the Don't list, and declare a `tools` list. The build, verify, debug, secure and review-and-ship reviewers get `Read`, `Grep`, `Glob`, `Bash` and `Write`, because they must run checks and show each command with its output; the harness, plan, design and learn reviewers get `Read`, `Grep`, `Glob` and `Write`. Every reviewer's rule is to write only its findings file and never edit the work under review. That is a prompt rule, not enforcement: Cursor subagents ignore `tools:` (they use readonly), so real enforcement needs hooks.

The human talks only to the [coordinator](coordinator.md). Loops run on their own, and human feedback comes only at the end of the cycle, where it feeds the Learn skills through [`/retro`](../commands/retro.md).
